sentences: You're standing on Plac Nowy, the New Square of Kazimierz.
Until the nineteenth century, a cluster of lanes and buildings stood here.
The square took its present shape in town plans of 1808 and 1844.
One side of it follows the line of the old defensive walls of Kazimierz.
The houses along that side once belonged to the Jewish hospital of the Kupa Synagogue.
In the middle stands the round market hall, built in 1900.
People call it the Okrąglak, the round one.
An inner hall is ringed by small shops on a twelve-sided plan, with an open-air passage in between.
In 1927, it was leased to the Jewish community, and it became a ritual poultry slaughterhouse.
After the war, it served as a market hall again.
On weekdays the square is still a market, for vegetables and for antiques.
It is also a place for festivals, among them concerts of the Jewish Culture Festival on the roof of the round hall.
Look at the round hall, and at its two entrances facing each other across it.

sentences: You're standing at the Church of Saint Catherine, known as the Augustinian Church.
It is a basilica with three naves, no tower and no transept.
Its stonework counts among the finest medieval stonework in Poland.
The king who founded Kazimierz brought the Augustinian friars here, and building began in 1342.
He wanted his new town to have a church as beautiful as the churches of Kraków next door.
The chancel was consecrated in 1378.
Then the ground shook.
In 1443, an earthquake brought down the vault of the nave, and it took until 1505 to rebuild it.
In 1786, another earthquake cracked the vault.
Soon after, the Austrians closed the friary and turned the church into an arms store, and later into a store for straw and hay.
In 1827, the city senate even planned to pull it down.
A committee for its renewal, set up in 1833, saved it.
Inside, the furnishings are modest, and that lets the clean lines of the architecture speak.
Before you go, look at the late Gothic porch, with its two richly carved stone portals.

Before you walk on, find the Well of Saint Stanislaus outside the church.
According to legend, the king threw the bishop's body into this well.
Water from the well flows from a fountain, for pilgrims to drink.
